title: Identification and Efficiency of Circular Dose-Shift Policy Values under Known Measurement Error
banked_reason: F2.5 final-reset hard stop: paper chooses κ₀ before varying δ, but Lean chooses κ₀ after δ; shift-independent amplitude is uncertified.
gap_reasons: The paper chooses κ₀ depending only on fixed class constants, before varying δ; Lean chooses κ₀ after δ, so paper implies Lean but Lean does not certify a shift-independent amplitude. Move ∃ κ₀ before ∀ δ.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery passed its field-tier review, and F2.5 accepted the repaired tangent-space setup; a separate study proved reusable torus marked-convolution lemmas in Causalean. The next F2.5 review found that the Lean packet construction chose κ₀ after δ although the paper requires one amplitude fixed before δ. The operator's final-reset rule stopped further re-encoding; F4/F5 and a complete Lean proof were not reached.
tldr: For a fixed nonzero circular dose shift observed through a known convolution channel, the note identifies the natural-law value under an explicit shift-mean bridge, a substantive premise not implied by pointwise exchangeability and consistency. At laws with nonvanishing channel multipliers it gives an exact support-sensitive adjoint-equation criterion for observed pathwise differentiability and the minimum influence-function variance. In the positive-binary fixed-Sobolev benchmark it proves the Fourier source criterion, sharp ordinary- and supersmooth minimax risks, matching honest-interval length rates, and attainment by the specified cross-fitted regularized estimator. The ordinary risk reaches the root-\(n\) scale at \(s=\beta+1/4\), without an endpoint Gaussian claim; in the strict interior \(s>\beta+1/4\), the estimator is asymptotically normal and efficient. Positivity and Sobolev algebra automatically supply the ordinary source condition when \(s\geq\beta\), so the interior efficiency theorem needs no separate source hypothesis.
gap: Modified-policy theory observes the natural dose; noisy-treatment work targets fixed-dose response curves; inverse theory treats abstract, linear, or quadratic functionals. None of the inspected sources resolves the law-dependent rational shift value with an observed outcome mark and learned denominator.
fill: Derive the support-sensitive regularity and efficiency frontier; prove the binary source criterion; close fixed-mean packet and fitted-denominator U-statistic bounds; and obtain sharp feasible estimation and honest-interval procedures.
